messages.subject: compare.multi.evol.rates strange results
parts:
Hello everyone, I am using the compare.multi.evol.rates function on 2D data derived from two different structures (A and B) of 8 species. As the instrucctions says, I superimposed this two shapes separately, then I concatenate the procrustes coordinates in a single array. The problem is that I got different results depending on the order I concatenate the two structures: compare.multi.evol.rates(c(AB)) != compare.multi.evol.rates(c(BA)

This is the way I concatenate the data:

gpa_c=array(data=NA,dim=c(dim(gpa_a$coords)[1]+dim(gpa_b$coords)[1],2,8))
gpa_c[1:dim(gpa_a$coords)[1],,]<-gpa_a$coords
gpa_c[dim(gpa_a$coords)[1]+1:dim(gpa_b$coords)[1],,]<-gpa_b$coords

I want to know if I am doing something wrong.

Thanks,

Juan

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] compare.multi.evol.rates strange results
parts:
Juan,

 

I have run a quick example, and results that should be the same in c(BA) vs c(AB) are in fact the same.  Specifically, the rate ratio remains the same, as do the individual rates for each subset (though they of course are reversed).

 

Significance levels should vary slightly, as they are based on permuting either dataset ‘A’ or dataset ‘B’.

 

Example code showing the equivalency between c(AB) and c(BA) is below.

 

Dean

 

###

library(geomorph)

 

data(plethspecies)

Y.gpa<-gpagen(plethspecies$land)

 

A <- two.d.array(Y.gpa$coords)

A1 <- A[,1:10];A2 <- A[,-(1:10)]

 

gp<-c(rep(1,10),rep(2,12))

gp2<-c(rep(1,12),rep(2,10))

 

EMR<-compare.multi.evol.rates(A=cbind(A1,A2),gp=gp, Subset=TRUE, phy= plethspecies$phy,iter=999)

EMR2<-compare.multi.evol.rates(A=cbind(A2,A1),gp=gp2, Subset=TRUE, phy= plethspecies$phy,iter=999)

 

summary(EMR)

summary(EMR2)

 

EMR3<-compare.multi.evol.rates(A=cbind(A1,A2),gp=gp, Subset=FALSE, phy= plethspecies$phy,iter=999)

EMR4<-compare.multi.evol.rates(A=cbind(A2,A1),gp=gp2, Subset=FALSE, phy= plethspecies$phy,iter=999)

 

summary(EMR3)

summary(EMR4)

Hello everyone, I am using the compare.multi.evol.rates function on 2D data derived from two different structures (A and B) of 8 species. As the instrucctions says, I superimposed this two shapes separately, then I concatenate the procrustes coordinates in a single array. The problem is that I got different results depending on the order I concatenate the two structures: compare.multi.evol.rates(c(AB)) != compare.multi.evol.rates(c(BA)

 

This is the way I concatenate the data:

 

gpa_c=array(data=NA,dim=c(dim(gpa_a$coords)[1]+dim(gpa_b$coords)[1],2,8))

gpa_c[1:dim(gpa_a$coords)[1],,]<-gpa_a$coords

gpa_c[dim(gpa_a$coords)[1]+1:dim(gpa_b$coords)[1],,]<-gpa_b$coords

 

I want to know if I am doing something wrong.

 

Thanks,

 

Juan

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] compare.multi.evol.rates strange results
parts:
Juan,

It might be a mistake in the way you are combining landmarks?  I just simulated an analysis like yours and got the same answer, irrespective of order.  Also, you can do this much easier with combine.subsets (see below)

Mike

> data("plethspecies")
> 
> A <- plethspecies$land
> B <- A + rnorm(length(A), 0.01)
> 
> AB <- combine.subsets(A, B, gpa = TRUE)
  |=======================================================================| 100%
  |=======================================================================| 100%
> BA <- combine.subsets(B, A, gpa = TRUE)
  |=======================================================================| 100%
  |=======================================================================| 100%
> 
> 
> gp <- factor(c(rep(1, 11), rep(2, 11)))
> dimnames(AB$coords)[[3]] <- dimnames(BA$coords)[[3]] <- dimnames(plethspecies$land)[[3]]
> 
> compare.multi.evol.rates(AB$coords, phy = plethspecies$phy, gp = gp)
  |=======================================================================| 100%

Call:


Observed Rate Ratio: 430.6486

P-value: 0.001

Based on 1000 random permutations

The rate for group 1 is 6.12544642916874e-06  

The rate for group 2 is 0.00263791481200038 > compare.multi.evol.rates(BA$coords, phy = plethspecies$phy, gp = gp)
  |=======================================================================| 100%
